material: Polished metal ring around a 2.7in glass display face; Google does not publish the alloy
features: Builds its own schedule by learning what you do — no programming
Soli radar wakes the 2.7in circular display as you walk up
Nest Temperature Sensor (2nd gen) in the box, up to 6 more supported
Power Sharing runs it with no C wire in most homes
Drives 3 stages plus humidifier, dehumidifier and ventilator

specs.voltageType: Low voltage 24V only — gas, electric, oil, forced air, heat pump and radiant. Will not run 120/240V baseboard or radiant electric heat
specs.cWireRequired: Not in most homes. Google's patented Power Sharing borrows power from the other wires, and the store page claims roughly 85% system compatibility — but it also states heating-only, cooling-only, zone-controlled and heat pump systems need a Nest Power Connector or a C wire
specs.cWireWorkaroundIncluded: No — the Nest Power Connector is a separate $24.99 accessory, not in the box
specs.heatCoolStages: Up to 3 stages of heating and cooling, plus fan speed control
specs.heatPumpSupport: Yes, including auxiliary and emergency heat
specs.accessoryTerminals: Humidifier, dehumidifier and ventilation (HRV/ERV) systems all supported — the widest accessory coverage of the Nest line
specs.remoteSensors: One Nest Temperature Sensor (2nd gen) included; up to 6 more. Google states all generations of the sensor work with this model
specs.occupancyDetection: Soli radar senses presence and proximity at the thermostat itself, plus phone-location Home/Away. The Nest Temperature Sensor reads temperature only — it does not detect occupancy
specs.matterSupport: Matter-certified, so it appears in any Matter app including Apple Home. Google does not publish a Thread radio for this model
specs.platforms: Google Home app (required for setup and control — the standalone Nest app is retired), Amazon Alexa, Apple Home via Matter
specs.utilityPrograms: Rush Hour Rewards, run by Renew Home with your energy provider, plus Nest Renew Energy Shift. Google's own help page says Rush Hour Rewards makes adjustments 'typically up to 4°F' for 3-4 hours during demand events; enrolment is through the Google Home app
specs.subscriptionRequired: No subscription. Learning, Savings Finder and Eco when Away are free, but a Google account and the Google Home app are mandatory

pros: The only thermostat here that genuinely writes its own schedule — install it and you can never open the app again
Runs without a C wire in most homes, which no ecobee, Sensi Touch 2, Amazon or Honeywell X-series model here can claim
Three stages plus humidifier, dehumidifier and ventilator terminals — the broadest HVAC coverage in this set alongside the ecobee Premium
Bundles a temperature sensor at a price where the $199.99 ecobee Enhanced bundles none
cons: 'No C wire required' carries a long asterisk: Google's own page lists heating-only, cooling-only, zone-controlled and heat pump systems as needing the $24.99 Nest Power Connector, which covers a large share of US homes
The bundled Nest Temperature Sensor is temperature-only — it cannot tell whether a room is occupied, which every ecobee SmartSensor can
Setup and control are locked to a Google account and the Google Home app; the old Nest app and Works with Nest are gone
Rush Hour Rewards pays you to let the utility push your setpoint by up to about 4°F for three to four hours at a time
Highest list price here at $279.99, on a 2-year warranty that both ecobee and Mysa beat
shortTagline: The only one that really learns your schedule, and it usually needs no C wire.

material: Mirrored polycarbonate front with a side touch strip; Google says the plastic parts are 49% recycled
features: Matter-certified, so it lands in Apple Home as well as Google and Alexa
Guided schedule setup in the Google Home app instead of learning
Two AAA cells back the display up if HVAC power drops
Quick Schedule and Savings Finder suggest tweaks after install
Side touch strip instead of the Learning Thermostat's rotating ring

specs.voltageType: Low voltage 24V only — furnaces, air conditioners, boilers and heat pumps. Not for 120/240V line-voltage heat
specs.cWireRequired: Not in most homes, but Google's own store page states heating-only, cooling-only, zone-controlled and heat pump systems need the Nest Power Connector or a C wire
specs.cWireWorkaroundIncluded: No — Nest Power Connector is a separate $24.99 accessory
specs.heatCoolStages: Google's tech-spec page lists conventional single-stage systems and heat pumps with auxiliary or emergency heat. Unlike the Learning Thermostat, it does not publish multi-stage conventional support
specs.heatPumpSupport: Yes, with auxiliary and emergency heat
specs.accessoryTerminals: Not published for this model. Google lists humidifier, dehumidifier and ventilator support only on the Learning Thermostat
specs.remoteSensors: None. Google states explicitly that the Nest Thermostat is not compatible with the Nest Temperature Sensor
specs.occupancyDetection: Built-in motion sensor at the thermostat plus phone-location Home/Away. No remote occupancy sensing of any kind
specs.matterSupport: Matter-certified — works with Google Home, Alexa and Apple Home
specs.platforms: Google Home app (required), Amazon Alexa, Apple Home via Matter
specs.utilityPrograms: Rush Hour Rewards and Nest Renew. Google's help page also notes Seasonal Savings currently supports the Nest Thermostat (2020) and Thermostat E, nudging setpoints up to 2°F over three weeks
specs.subscriptionRequired: No subscription, but a Google account and the Google Home app are required

pros: Matter certification at $129.99 puts it in Apple Home, which no ecobee, Sensi or Amazon model here manages
Same Power Sharing wiring trick as the Learning Thermostat, so it usually installs without a C wire
Battery backup on two AAA cells — the Amazon, X2S and Sensi Touch 2 all go dark if 24V power drops
Cheapest way into the Google ecosystem with a real touch UI, at less than half the Learning Thermostat's list price
cons: No remote sensor support at all — Google says outright it is not compatible with the Nest Temperature Sensor, so this is a one-room thermostat
It does not learn. Google gives it guided schedule setup instead, which is the single feature people think they are buying when they buy 'a Nest'
Google's spec page only claims single-stage conventional support; two-stage furnace owners should check compatibility before buying
No published humidifier, dehumidifier or ventilator terminals
1-year warranty, against 2 on the Learning Thermostat and 3 on every ecobee here
shortTagline: Matter-certified and usually C-wire-free, but it does not learn and takes no sensors.

material: Black glass front in a die-cast zinc alloy frame
features: Power Extender Kit in the box — no C wire needed if you have R, W, Y and G
SmartSensor in the box; up to 32 pair, each sensing temperature and occupancy
Radar occupancy and proximity sensing built into the thermostat
Indoor air quality monitor with alerts and guidance
Alexa built in with speaker and mic, or Siri via Apple HomeKit

specs.voltageType: Low voltage 24VAC — furnaces, air conditioners, heat pumps, boilers, PTAC and fan coil units. Not for 120/240V line-voltage heat
specs.cWireRequired: Not in practice. ecobee ships the Power Extender Kit in the box, which synthesises a common wire from R, W, Y and G at the furnace. Direct wiring uses C and Rc if you do have five wires
specs.cWireWorkaroundIncluded: Yes — Power Extender Kit included. The same kit is a $24.99 extra on the Essential
specs.heatCoolStages: 2H/2C conventional; boilers, PTAC and fan coil units with up to 3 fan speeds
specs.heatPumpSupport: Yes — heat pump 2H/2C plus 2 stages of auxiliary heat, the deepest heat-pump staging in this set
specs.accessoryTerminals: One 1-wire or one 2-wire accessory on the ACC+/ACC− terminals: humidifier, dehumidifier or HRV/ERV ventilator
specs.remoteSensors: One SmartSensor in the box; up to 32 pair, over a 915MHz radio at up to 60 ft. Extra sensors are $99.99 for a 2-pack
specs.occupancyDetection: Radar occupancy and proximity in the thermostat, and every SmartSensor also detects occupancy over a 140° x 100° field to about 20 ft
specs.matterSupport: Not shipping on this model. ecobee's own spec page lists HomeKit, Alexa, Google Assistant, SmartThings and IFTTT and never mentions Matter; third-party write-ups describe a phased rollout, so treat Matter as unconfirmed here
specs.platforms: Apple HomeKit with Siri, Alexa built in (speaker and microphone), Google Assistant, Samsung SmartThings, IFTTT
specs.utilityPrograms: eco+ Community Energy Savings with 150+ North American utilities. ecobee states events move your temperature 1-4°F for no more than a few hours, a handful of times a year, and you can opt out of any event from the app; some programs pay an enrolment rebate up to $125
specs.subscriptionRequired: No subscription for eco+, energy reports, remote sensors or scheduling. ecobee Smart Security — the intrusion-monitoring layer on the same hardware — is the paid tier

pros: The Power Extender Kit is in the box, so the C-wire problem is solved at purchase rather than at $25 extra or a $200 electrician call
Heat pump 2H/2C plus two auxiliary stages beats every other thermostat here on staging depth
SmartSensors detect occupancy as well as temperature — Google's, Honeywell's cheaper models' and Sensi's sensors mostly do not
Built-in speaker and mic make it a working Alexa device, and it doubles as an ecobee Smart Security hub
3-year warranty, a year longer than Google and Resideo
cons: No Matter. ecobee's own spec sheet lists HomeKit, Alexa, Google, SmartThings and IFTTT and nothing else, which is a strange gap on a $260 flagship in 2026
$259.99 is the second-highest price here and it went up — ecobee has quietly raised list prices across the range
The air-quality monitor produces a score and advice, not a calibrated PM2.5 or VOC reading you can act on
Alexa built in means an always-listening mic on your hallway wall, with no hardware mute switch of the kind Echo speakers have
Only one accessory circuit — a humidifier and an ERV cannot both be wired at once
shortTagline: Best sensors and deepest heat-pump staging here — and still no Matter in 2026.

material: Black glass front with a plastic frame
features: Power Extender Kit in the box, same as the Premium
Radar occupancy and proximity sensing built in — the Essential has none
Same 4in 540x540 touchscreen as the Premium
One-wire accessory terminal for a humidifier, dehumidifier or ventilator
Works with up to 32 SmartSensors, sold separately

specs.voltageType: Low voltage 24VAC — furnaces, air conditioners, heat pumps, boilers, PTAC and fan coil units. Not for 120/240V line-voltage heat
specs.cWireRequired: Not in practice — the Power Extender Kit is included and creates a common wire from R, W, Y and G
specs.cWireWorkaroundIncluded: Yes — Power Extender Kit included in the box
specs.heatCoolStages: 2H/2C conventional; boilers, PTAC and fan coil units
specs.heatPumpSupport: Yes — heat pump 2H/2C plus 1 stage of auxiliary heat (the Premium gets 2)
specs.accessoryTerminals: One 1-wire accessory: humidifier, dehumidifier or HRV/ERV ventilator. The Premium's 2-wire option is not available here
specs.remoteSensors: None in the box. Up to 32 SmartSensors pair, sold separately at $99.99 for a 2-pack
specs.occupancyDetection: Radar occupancy and proximity in the thermostat. Room-level occupancy needs SmartSensors you have to buy
specs.matterSupport: Not listed on ecobee's spec page for this model
specs.platforms: Apple HomeKit with Siri, Amazon Alexa, Samsung SmartThings and IFTTT are what ecobee's spec page lists; ecobee's retail listing also claims Google Assistant. No built-in microphone or speaker
specs.utilityPrograms: eco+ Community Energy Savings with 150+ utilities; enrolled events shift your temperature 1-4°F for a few hours a handful of times a year, opt-out per event
specs.subscriptionRequired: No subscription. A free ecobee account is required

pros: Same screen, same radar occupancy sensor and the same in-the-box Power Extender Kit as the $259.99 Premium, for $60 less
Handles heat pump 2H/2C with aux, which is more staging than the Nest Thermostat, X2S, Sensi Lite or Amazon can manage
Still takes 32 occupancy-sensing SmartSensors if you add them later
3-year warranty
cons: No SmartSensor in the box — buy one and the price gap to the Premium closes to almost nothing
No air quality monitor, no speaker and no built-in Alexa or Siri voice
One auxiliary heat stage instead of the Premium's two, which matters on cold-climate heat pumps
No Matter on ecobee's spec list, so Matter-only smart home setups are out
Only one 1-wire accessory circuit, so a humidifier and a ventilator cannot both be driven
shortTagline: The Premium's screen, radar and power kit for $60 less — you just supply your own sensor.

colorOptions: Black front with white sides and back
material: Plastic body with a 2.8in colour LCD touchscreen
features: Wi-Fi 6 radio — newer than the Premium's dual-band 802.11ac
2.8in full-colour touchscreen at an entry price
Works with up to 32 ecobee SmartSensors (2nd gen or newer)
Apple HomeKit, Alexa and Google Assistant with no hub
Same 3-year ecobee warranty as the Premium

specs.voltageType: Low voltage 24VAC gas, oil and electric forced-air systems. Not for 120/240V line-voltage heat
specs.cWireRequired: Yes — powered through the C and R terminals. This is the ecobee that does not include the fix
specs.cWireWorkaroundIncluded: No. The Power Extender Kit that ships free with the Premium and Enhanced is a $24.99 accessory here, and the trim plate is another $14.99
specs.heatCoolStages: 2H/1C or 1H/2C conventional. The single OB terminal doubles as W2 or Y2, so you get one extra stage in total, not two
specs.heatPumpSupport: Yes, heat pump 2H/1C. No second compressor stage
specs.accessoryTerminals: None. There is no ACC terminal, so no humidifier, dehumidifier or ventilator control
specs.remoteSensors: None in the box. Up to 32 SmartSensors (2nd gen or newer) pair, sold separately. ecobee states the original ecobee Room Sensor is not compatible
specs.occupancyDetection: None built in — the Essential drops the radar occupancy sensor that the Premium and Enhanced have. Occupancy-based eco+ features need a SmartSensor you buy separately
specs.matterSupport: Not listed on ecobee's spec page for this model
specs.platforms: Apple HomeKit, Amazon Alexa, Google Assistant. No built-in voice, no speaker
specs.utilityPrograms: eco+ Community Energy Savings with 150+ utilities; enrolled demand events move your setpoint 1-4°F for a few hours, with per-event opt-out
specs.subscriptionRequired: No subscription. A free ecobee account is required

pros: Cheapest route into ecobee's SmartSensor ecosystem — 32 occupancy-sensing sensors will pair to a $140 thermostat
Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth LE 5.4 make it the most modern radio stack in this comparison
3-year warranty at $139.99, which beats Google's 1-year on the similarly priced Nest Thermostat
Full colour touchscreen rather than the monochrome or button-driven UI at this price from Resideo and Copeland
cons: The Power Extender Kit that comes free with both bigger ecobees costs $24.99 here, so a C-wire-less home pays $165 not $140
The radar occupancy sensor is gone — the Essential cannot tell whether you are in the room without a $50 SmartSensor
No accessory terminal at all: no humidifier, dehumidifier or ventilator control
Heat pump support stops at 2H/1C, so cold-climate multi-stage systems are out
Launched at $129.99 in March 2025 and now lists at $139.99 — an eight percent rise in the first year
shortTagline: The cheapest way into ecobee's sensors — but it is the ecobee that omits the C-wire kit.

material: White plastic with a capacitive front panel; trim plate included
features: Built with Honeywell Home thermostat technology under Amazon's badge
Alexa Hunches turn the setpoint down when Alexa decides you are out
Energy Dashboard inside the Alexa app
Trim plate included, unlike the Sensi Touch 2
Comfort zones can take temperature readings from select Echo devices

specs.voltageType: Low voltage 24V — Amazon lists conventional forced air, heat pump and radiant boiler. It does not work with 110-240V systems
specs.cWireRequired: Yes, hard requirement. Every Amazon, Best Buy and utility-store listing is titled 'C-wire required'
specs.cWireWorkaroundIncluded: No — the C-Wire Power Adapter is a separate purchase, or you buy the bundle SKU instead of this one
specs.heatCoolStages: Not published by Amazon. The listings say only 'most 24V heating and cooling systems (conventional forced air, heat pump, radiant boiler)' with no stage count anywhere — run Amazon's compatibility checker before buying
specs.heatPumpSupport: Listed as compatible with heat pumps. Amazon does not publish how it handles auxiliary or emergency heat
specs.accessoryTerminals: None published, and no humidifier, dehumidifier or ventilator control is advertised anywhere in the listing
specs.remoteSensors: No dedicated remote sensor exists for this thermostat. Best Buy's listing states comfort zones can use select Echo devices or the Amazon Smart Air Quality Monitor as temperature inputs instead
specs.occupancyDetection: None at the thermostat. Away behaviour comes entirely from Alexa Hunches
specs.platforms: Amazon Alexa only. No Google Home, no Apple Home, no HomeKit, no SmartThings. The Alexa app is mandatory and most settings are not reachable on the thermostat screen at all
specs.utilityPrograms: ENERGY STAR certified and one of the most heavily rebated thermostats in US utility marketplaces; several utilities bundle it into demand-response enrolment
specs.subscriptionRequired: No subscription, but an Amazon account and the Alexa app are required and there is no web dashboard

pros: $79.99 list, frequently discounted to $50-60, and rebated by more US utilities than almost anything else here
Honeywell Home hardware underneath, so the relay and wiring side is Resideo-grade rather than a no-name design
Alexa Hunches away-control works without you configuring a schedule at all
Trim plate included in the box, which Copeland charges extra for on the Sensi Touch 2
cons: A C wire is a hard requirement and the adapter is not in the box — the real cost in a four-wire home is the thermostat plus an adapter
Alexa only. There is no Google Home, no Apple Home, no HomeKit and no Matter, so it is a dead end outside Amazon's ecosystem
Most settings are not on the thermostat itself; without a phone and the Alexa app you can barely configure it
No remote sensors of any kind — the Echo comfort-zone workaround is not the same as a real room sensor
Amazon publishes no stage count, no accessory terminals and no wiring detail, so multi-stage and heat-pump owners are buying blind
shortTagline: Cheap, Honeywell-built and heavily rebated — but Alexa-only, and a C wire is required.

material: Plastic housing with a 5in customisable colour touchscreen
features: 5in touchscreen, the largest display in this comparison
Up to 20 wireless room sensors per home with 200ft range
Onboard radar occupancy plus presence detection in the sensors
Shows Ring and First Alert VX1 doorbell feeds on the thermostat
Free C-Wire Adapter by mail-in voucher in the box

specs.voltageType: Low voltage 24V. Home Depot's listing states plainly that it does not work with 120-240V electric baseboard heat
specs.cWireRequired: Yes — Resideo states the X8S needs a constant 24V supply through a common wire
specs.cWireWorkaroundIncluded: Not in the box, but Home Depot's listing says the package contains a voucher for a free mail-in Honeywell Home C-Wire Adapter
specs.heatCoolStages: Sources conflict: Resideo's own product page says up to 4 Heat/2 Cool on heat pumps or 3 Heat/4 Cool conventional, while Home Depot's listing for the same product says up to 3 Heat/2 Cool heat pump or 2 Heat/2 Cool conventional
specs.heatPumpSupport: Yes, heat pump with electric backup
specs.accessoryTerminals: Resideo advertises 'advanced indoor air quality control' but notes additional HVAC equipment may be required, and publishes no plain humidifier/dehumidifier/ventilator terminal list
specs.remoteSensors: One wireless room sensor is included with the X8VMC9W and X8VWF10B SKUs only — not with this one. Up to 20 sensors per home, 200ft range, $44.99 each
specs.occupancyDetection: Yes — onboard radar in the thermostat plus occupancy and presence detection in the room sensors
specs.matterSupport: Matter certified, but shallow. Matter Alpha's review found the air quality readings the thermostat measures are not exposed over Matter at all, and scheduling still has to happen on the thermostat or in the First Alert app
specs.platforms: First Alert app by Resideo (required — you cannot generate the Matter pairing code without it), Amazon Alexa, Google Assistant, Apple Home via Matter
specs.utilityPrograms: ENERGY STAR certified and rebate-eligible; Resideo pitches enrolment in utility energy-management programs
specs.subscriptionRequired: No subscription for thermostat features. A First Alert account is required, and Resideo ships several different apps which reviewers found confusing

pros: Up to 20 room sensors at 200ft range — more sensor coverage than any other thermostat in this comparison bar the ecobees
5in colour touchscreen with a customisable idle screen, and it can display a Ring or First Alert doorbell feed
Radar occupancy in the thermostat plus presence detection in each sensor, at $40 under the ecobee Premium
The C-Wire Adapter is free — by mail-in voucher — where Amazon, Copeland and ecobee's Essential all charge for theirs
cons: Matter support is thin: air quality data is not exposed over Matter at all and you still cannot schedule through it
You must install the First Alert app just to generate the Matter code, which defeats much of the point of Matter
Resideo's own page and Home Depot's listing give different stage counts for the same thermostat — verify against your system before buying
The free C-wire adapter is a mail-in voucher, not a part in the box, so a C-wire-less install stalls until it arrives
Reviewers hit setup failures at launch and found the doorbell integration buried and limited to Ring and First Alert VX1
shortTagline: Biggest screen and 20 room sensors, over a deliberately minimal Matter layer.

material: Plastic housing with a 4.84 sq in monochrome display and a UWP wall plate
features: Matter certified at $79.99 — the cheapest Matter thermostat here
UWP wall plate mounting shared with Resideo's professional range
Flexible 7-day, 5-1-1, 5-2 or 1-week scheduling
Geofencing away control through the First Alert app
Replaces the long-running RTH6580WF

specs.voltageType: Low voltage 24V. Resideo states it does not work with electric baseboard heat at 120-240V
specs.cWireRequired: Yes, hard requirement. Resideo states a constant 24V C-wire supply is needed and the X2S is not battery powered
specs.cWireWorkaroundIncluded: No adapter of any kind is included
specs.heatPumpSupport: Yes — up to 2 Heat/1 Cool heat pump with electric backup
specs.accessoryTerminals: None published. Humidity is monitored and displayed, not controlled
specs.remoteSensors: None. There is no room sensor option for this model
specs.occupancyDetection: None. Away behaviour comes from geofencing in the First Alert app
specs.matterSupport: Matter certified — but Matter Alpha's reviewer could see temperature, humidity and mode in SmartThings and could not get setpoint changes to take effect, which breaks the automations Matter is meant to enable
specs.platforms: First Alert app by Resideo (required for setup and to generate the Matter code), Amazon Alexa, Google Assistant, Apple Home via Matter
specs.utilityPrograms: ENERGY STAR certified. Resideo's launch materials specifically call out enabling enrolment in utility energy-management programs
specs.subscriptionRequired: No subscription. A First Alert account is required

pros: Matter certified, ENERGY STAR certified and dual-band Wi-Fi for $79.99 — nothing else here does all three that cheaply
2H/2C conventional staging is more than the similarly priced Sensi Lite or the Nest Thermostat publish
Mounts on Resideo's UWP plate, the same system professional installers use, which makes wiring tidy
2-year warranty at $80, double what Amazon and Google give at this price
cons: A C wire is mandatory and no adapter is included — in a four-wire house this $80 thermostat becomes an electrician's callout
Matter works only for reading state in at least one reviewer's testing: setpoint changes sent over Matter did not stick
You have to install the First Alert app to get a Matter pairing code, so Matter does not free you from the vendor app
No room sensors and no occupancy sensing at all — this is strictly a one-room thermostat
No humidifier, dehumidifier or ventilator control
shortTagline: The cheapest Matter thermostat here, if you have a C wire and forgive its thin Matter.

material: Plastic housing with a colour touchscreen and a beveled bezel
features: Heat pump staging up to 4 Heat / 2 Cool
ACC+/ACC- terminals for humidifier and dehumidifier control
Sensi Room Sensors for averaged multi-room temperature
Geofencing from your phone's location
Copeland states it does not sell your data to third parties

specs.voltageType: Low voltage 24VAC — gas, oil, electric, heat pump, boilers. Not for 120/240V line-voltage heat
specs.cWireRequired: Yes. Copeland's spec sheet requires 20-30VAC between RH/RC and C, and every retail listing is labelled 'C-Wire Required'
specs.cWireWorkaroundIncluded: No — the Sensi C-Wire Kit is a separate purchase at roughly $28
specs.heatCoolStages: 1H/1C, 2H/2C multi-stage, and up to 4H/2C on heat pumps
specs.heatPumpSupport: Yes — up to 4 heat and 2 cool including auxiliary stages, the widest heat-pump staging here alongside the ecobee Premium
specs.accessoryTerminals: ACC+/ACC- terminals drive a humidifier or dehumidifier, with a humidify range of 5-50% RH and dehumidify 40-95% RH

specs.matterSupport: No. TechHive states the Touch 2 supports neither Matter nor Apple HomeKit
specs.platforms: Sensi app, Amazon Alexa, Google Assistant and Samsung SmartThings. No Apple Home

pros: 4H/2C heat pump staging plus humidifier and dehumidifier terminals — genuinely serious HVAC coverage for under $200
3-year warranty and a published privacy stance that no other brand here makes explicit
Street price has settled around $189 against a $209.99 list, and it periodically drops much further
Real multi-stage and dual-fuel handling that the similarly priced Nest Thermostat and ecobee Essential do not offer
cons: No Matter and no Apple HomeKit — the Touch 2 dropped the HomeKit support the original Sensi Touch had
C wire required and the C-Wire Kit is a ~$28 extra, where ecobee includes an equivalent kit free

material: Plastic housing with a glass touchscreen face
features: Runs without a C wire on most conventional systems
Ten terminals including AUX, L and dual-fuel support
2.4GHz Wi-Fi plus Bluetooth LE for setup
Geofencing and flexible scheduling in the Sensi app
3-year limited warranty per Home Depot's specification table

specs.remoteSensors: None. Copeland states only the Sensi Touch 2 works with Sensi Room Sensors
specs.occupancyDetection: None. Away control is geofencing from your phone only
specs.platforms: Sensi app, Amazon Alexa, Google Assistant, Samsung SmartThings. No Apple Home
specs.utilityPrograms: ENERGY STAR certified, rated for about 23% HVAC energy savings, and stocked across US utility rebate marketplaces

pros: One of only three thermostats here that runs without a C wire on ordinary conventional systems, and by far the cheapest
Ten terminals including AUX and L, with dual-fuel and zone-valve support that no other sub-$100 model here documents
Copeland spells out the C-wire exception in the product title itself instead of burying it in a compatibility checker
$79 street against $89.99 list, with heavy utility-marketplace rebate availability
cons: The C-wire exemption evaporates exactly where it matters: heat-only, cool-only and heat pump systems all need one
No Apple Home and no Matter, so it is Alexa, Google or the Sensi app and nothing else

No humidifier or ventilator terminals despite the generous terminal count

material: Moulded plastic body with a glass faceplate and capacitive touch controls
features: Line voltage: 120V or 240V, 16A, 3,800W at 240V

Humidity sensor plus light and proximity sensors

5-year warranty on Mysa's own product page

specs.voltageType: Line voltage 120V or 240V AC, 16A maximum — 3,800W at 240V or 1,900W at 120V, on a 20A breaker. This is the opposite of every 24V thermostat here; a low-voltage model will not run baseboard heat and this will not run a furnace
specs.cWireRequired: Not applicable — line-voltage thermostats have no C wire. It does need both line conductors (L1 and L2/neutral) present in the box, so a two-wire switch loop will not work
specs.heatCoolStages: Heating only, on/off line-voltage switching. No cooling and no staging
specs.heatPumpSupport: No. Mysa states it does not work with 24V furnaces or central air, millivolt systems, central hydronic boilers, or electric in-floor heating, which needs a different Mysa product
specs.remoteSensors: None. Mysa's model is one thermostat per heater circuit, so each room is its own zone rather than a sensor network
specs.occupancyDetection: Light and proximity sensors wake and dim the display on the V2. Away control is app geofencing. There is no room occupancy sensing
specs.matterSupport: Not listed for the baseboard models. Mysa's own Matter article covers the central-HVAC Smart Thermostat and says Matter is 'expected in early 2026 via firmware update'
specs.platforms: Mysa app, Apple HomeKit, Amazon Alexa, Google Home
specs.utilityPrograms: Mysa states both baseboard models support utility demand-response programs, and the V2 is stocked across US utility rebate marketplaces
specs.subscriptionRequired: No subscription — Mysa markets the app as 100% free

pros: One of the very few smart thermostats that actually controls 120/240V electric baseboard heat, which no Nest, ecobee, Sensi or Honeywell model here can touch
Real energy monitoring in watts per heater, so you can see which room is eating the bill
Apple HomeKit, Alexa and Google support with no hub, on a 5-year warranty
One thermostat per heater means genuine per-room zoning without buying a sensor ecosystem
cons: 16A / 3,800W ceiling at 240V, and it needs both L1 and L2 in the box — a two-wire switch loop or an oversized heater bank is a hard no
Heating only, on/off. No cooling, no staging, no humidifier, no ventilator
No Matter. Mysa's Matter rollout is documented for the central-HVAC thermostat, not the baseboard line
Warranty sources conflict: Mysa's own page claims 5 years while SupplyHouse's listing for MYSA-V2-0 says 2
You need one per heater circuit, so a four-room apartment is four thermostats and four installs
shortTagline: The default smart thermostat for electric baseboard heat — and it will not run a furnace.

model: Mysa Smart Thermostat LITE for Electric Baseboard Heaters
material: Moulded plastic faceplate with physical clickable buttons
features: Same 120-240V, 16A, 3,800W switching as the V2
Smallest line-voltage smart thermostat here at 4.4 x 3 x 0.6in
Physical buttons instead of a touchscreen
Apple HomeKit, Alexa and Google Home with no hub
5-year warranty at under $100

specs.voltageType: Line voltage 120V or 240V AC, 16A maximum — 3,800W at 240V or 1,900W at 120V, identical to the V2. Not compatible with any 24V system
specs.cWireRequired: Not applicable — line voltage. Both line conductors must be present in the gang box
specs.heatCoolStages: Heating only, on/off line-voltage switching. No cooling and no staging
specs.heatPumpSupport: No. Same exclusions as the V2: no 24V furnaces or central air, no millivolt, no central hydronic boilers, no electric in-floor heating
specs.remoteSensors: None. One thermostat per heater circuit
specs.occupancyDetection: None. The LITE drops the V2's light and proximity sensors entirely, and there is no humidity sensor either. Away control is app geofencing
specs.matterSupport: Not listed for the baseboard models
specs.platforms: Mysa app, Apple HomeKit, Amazon Alexa, Google Home
specs.utilityPrograms: Mysa states the LITE supports utility demand-response programs and it is stocked in US utility rebate marketplaces

pros: Under $100 for a real line-voltage smart thermostat with HomeKit, Alexa and Google support and a 5-year warranty
Identical 16A / 3,800W switching capability to the $159 V2 — you lose features, not capacity
Physically the smallest thermostat here, which matters when you are fitting several in one apartment
Launched at $109 in 2023 and now sells for $99, one of the few products here whose price has gone down
cons: No energy monitoring, no humidity sensor and no light or proximity sensors — the V2's whole value-add is stripped out
Buttons rather than a touchscreen, and Mysa's app carries most of the configuration
Heating only. No cooling, no staging, no accessory control
No Matter on the baseboard line
Still one unit per heater circuit, so a whole-home baseboard retrofit is a multi-hundred-dollar project
shortTagline: Baseboard control under $100: same switching as the V2, none of its sensors.
